content.text:
## Verdict: NEEDS REWORK

The core PromQL is correct (I verified associativity, set-operator `on` legality, and label propagation), D4's asymmetry argument is genuinely right, and the masked-replica fixture really does double as the D4 guard. But D3's case table omits a scenario that turns this into a **new false page on healthy infrastructure**, §3.5's fixture instructions silently destroy the existing `== 0`-vs-`>= 0` mutation guard, all three §4.2 assertions are structurally unfalsifiable under `sum_metric_from`'s semantics, and D1's naming rationale rests on a factually wrong claim about Postgres `NOTIFY`. None are hard to fix, but each would ship green.

## Findings

### BLOCKER

- **D3's table misses the new-instance case; job-scoping the controls creates a false page on a healthy replica** — `drained` moving from `by (job, instance)` to `by (job)` (D3/D4) removes the per-instance gate that today keeps a *brand-new* replica out of the alert. Concretely: notifying work happens at t=0…5m; a replica is created at t=6m (k8s pod → **new `instance` label → fresh series**, unlike a same-host restart, which Prometheus sees as a counter reset on a continuous series and which therefore stays protected); no further notifying work until t=40m. At t=21m the new replica has `increase(notifications[30m]) == 0` (true since birth), while `sum by (job)` of both controls is `> 0` from the t=0…5m burst on its neighbours. `for: 15m` elapses and the alert fires on a perfectly healthy replica, blaming a pooler. Under the current expression that replica's own `increase(drained[30m])` is 0 (the rows were already published before it existed), so it cannot fire. | Why it matters: this is a *new* false positive on the exact workload profile SMA-495 exists to protect (quiet deployment, bursty maintenance traffic), and it happens on every scale-up/rolling deploy that lands in a lull. It also invalidates the shipped `for: 15m` rationale at `ops/observability/prometheus/rules/iam.rules.yml:57-62`, which bounds the transient at "~2 minutes" precisely because the control was per-instance — §3.4 lists only two claims in that comment as changing, not this third one. | Suggested fix: add a fourth conjunct restricting the alert to instances that existed for the whole window — `and on (job, instance) (iam_outbox_listener_notifications_total offset 30m)` (set operators only test presence, so no comparison is needed; the 5m staleness lookback makes this "had a sample in [T-35m, T-30m]"). Add a promtool block with a series that starts at t=10m and assert it never appears in `exp_alerts`. Rewrite the `for: 15m` paragraph accordingly, and add the row to D3's table.

- **§3.5's "enqueues: added" is under-specified per job, and one plausible reading kills the `== 0` → `>= 0` mutation guard** — the first fixture block has three jobs (`iam`, `iam-healthy`, `iam-idle`, `ops/observability/prometheus/rules/tests/iam.test.yml:110-134`) and the table gives one undifferentiated instruction. If the implementer adds the enqueues series only to `job="iam"` (the firing target — the minimum needed to make the block still pass), then under a `>= 0` mutant `iam-healthy`'s LHS becomes true but `sum by (job) (increase(enqueues[30m]))` for `job="iam-healthy"` is an **empty vector**, `and on (job)` drops it, no alert is produced, and the mutant passes. | Why it matters: `iam-healthy` is the single guard the fixture comment at `iam.test.yml:91-94` calls MANDATORY, and AC4 asserts "the pre-existing blocks still assert what they asserted before" — which would be false, silently. | Suggested fix: specify the series per job explicitly: `iam` climbing, `iam-healthy` **climbing** (this is what keeps the `>= 0` guard alive), `iam-idle` flat-at-zero or absent. Add "the `>= 0` mutant must still be caught by `iam-healthy`" to §4.1's manual-mutation proof list.

- **All three §4.2 assertions are vacuous as specified** — `support::sum_metric_from` (`rs/crates/services/paigasus-iam/tests/support/mod.rs:751-759`) filters lines by name and sums; an **absent** family sums to `0.0`, identically to a family present at zero. Test 2 ("Gated") extends `wake_on_commit_false_emits_no_notification` (`tests/relay_nudge_pg.rs:530-552`), which (a) installs **no recorder at all**, so every `counter!()` in the process is a no-op, and (b) constructs only `PgOutbox::new(false)`, so under D5 the family is never primed and never exists. `assert_eq!(sum_metric_from(&out, "…notifying_enqueues_total"), 0.0)` therefore passes with the entire feature deleted. Restate AC2 as "primed iff `[outbox].wake_on_commit = true`", which is what D5's stated meaning ("this replica is configured to nudge") actually says.

- **§4.2's isolation claim describes a mechanism that does not exist** — "Each test therefore calls `paigasus_observability::init` with its own recorder name and renders through its own handle". `init` is `HANDLE.get_or_init(...).clone()` (`rs/crates/libs/paigasus-observability/src/lib.rs:22-40`); the `service` argument is used **only for a log line**, and a second call returns a clone of the *first* handle over the *same* registry. The isolation comes entirely from nextest's process-per-test — which I confirmed is how `:test` runs (`.moon/tasks/rust.yml:22-24`, `cargo nextest run --no-tests=pass`). | Why it matters: an implementer reading this will believe per-test names buy isolation and may add a second exact-value test to the same binary that then interferes under any non-nextest invocation. | Suggested fix: delete the "own recorder name / own handle" clause; keep only "nextest gives each test its own process; these assertions are invalid under bare `cargo test`", matching `support/mod.rs:747-749`.

- **The `iam-idle` fixture comment becomes false and §3.5 does not require rewriting it** — `iam.test.yml:96-104` states that "ONLY the right-hand `(drained[30m]) > 0` term keeps it silent", verified by hand. After the change, if `iam-idle` gets no enqueues series (or a flat one), the enqueues control also keeps it silent, so deleting the drained clause no longer flips it — the comment claims a discriminating power it no longer has. That is the exact SMA-466 lesson recorded in the `IamAuthzRedisCacheBypassed` block (`iam.test.yml:343-356`). | Why it matters: a fixture comment that lies is how the next reviewer gets misled into deleting a real guard. | Suggested fix: add the `iam-idle` comment rewrite to §3.5's file list and to AC4, pointing forward to the new rollback-storm block as the drained clause's guard.

### MINOR

- **No `eval_time` specified for the two new blocks** — with `for: 15m`, a block that only asserts `exp_alerts: []` at, say, `10m` passes vacuously and the "delete the control → this block fires" proof in §4.1 will not reproduce. Specify `eval_time: 35m` (matching the existing blocks at `iam.test.yml:130`).
- **The first block's new enqueues series must climb from t=0** — the `eval_time: 10m` empty assertion is the only thing pinning `for: 15m` (`iam.test.yml:105-109`), and it discriminates only because the condition is true from t=1m. An enqueues series that starts climbing later silently destroys that guard. Specify `0+5x40`.
- **Fixture series must carry the same `job` label** — several existing blocks write unlabelled series (e.g. `iam.test.yml:38-39`, `:72-73`). An enqueues series added without `job="…"` gives `sum by (job)` an empty `job` value, `and on (job)` finds no match, and the block goes silent for a reason no one will guess. Worth one sentence in §3.5.
- **§5 "Files touched" misses in-repo drift** — (a) `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-observability.md:654` ("Both terms aggregate `by (job, instance)`, so this fires per replica") is now wrong; (b) `docs/ops/RUNBOOK-observability.md:680-684`'s `wake_on_commit = false` paragraph gains a second structural-silence reason (the enqueue counter is also never registered); (c) `main.rs:435-444`'s `describe_iam_metrics` doc comment enumerates the families it covers; (d) the replay-inert test needs a parked-row seeder — `seed_parked` is a private helper in `tests/dead_letters_pg.rs:41-55`, so either that file, `tests/support/mod.rs`, or a duplicated helper must be listed.
- **AC2's second half has no test** — "absent from `/metrics` entirely rather than present at zero" is asserted nowhere in §4.2, and `sum_metric_from` cannot express it (it returns `0.0` either way); it needs a `!out.contains(name)` assertion or the AC should be dropped.
- **A zero-code alternative is not considered or rejected** — `(sum by (job) (increase(iam_outbox_relay_drained_total[30m])) - sum by (job) (increase(iam_outbox_dead_letters_replayed_total[30m]))) > 0` needs no new metric, no binary change, and no rules/binary coupling. It is worse (replays are counted post-commit and in a different window than they are drained; a re-parked-and-re-replayed row double-subtracts), but the spec should say so rather than skip it.

### QUESTIONS

- Does every replica scraped under `job="iam"` necessarily share one Postgres instance and therefore one `NOTIFY` broadcast domain? `sum by (job)` assumes it. If a job ever spans shards/regions/databases, replica A's enqueues would license an alert on replica B, which is the same defect as the new-instance case but permanent.
- `relay_enabled = false` + `wake_on_commit = true` is accepted config (warned about at `main.rs:38-40`) and `PgOutbox::new(cfg.outbox.wake_on_commit)` is **not** gated on `relay_enabled` — so that deployment emits and primes the new counter while running no listener and no relay. Intended? It should at least be named in the counter's doc.
- Why is the pre-commit imprecision (D2) worth carrying at all, given that the rollback storm it guards against necessarily also trips `IamHighErrorRate` at critical? Making the counter post-commit was rejected as "changes a core port for one alert control signal" — but D3's second conjunct is itself machinery added for the same one signal, and it costs a silence path (see MAJOR above).
- What is the intended deploy order for `ops/observability/**` relative to the IAM binary in this project, and is there any gate that would catch "this alert's controls have been structurally empty for a week"?

## What's good

- **D4 is right, and I verified the mechanics.** `and`/`or`/`unless` accept `on(...)`; `and` is left-associative at the same precedence as `unless`; `and` returns the LHS elements **with the LHS's labels intact**, so `{job, instance}` survives and `{{ $labels.instance }}` in the annotation still resolves; and many-LHS-to-one-RHS is legal for set operators (no `group_left`, which is in fact forbidden here). The asymmetry — per-instance left term, per-job controls — is the correct call and is argued from the right premise (`NOTIFY` is broadcast; a notifying enqueue is not).
- **The masked-replica block genuinely doubles as the D4 guard, as claimed.** With enqueues on `healthy` only, the correct rule yields `{job=iam, instance=wedged:8080}`; the `by (job, instance)` mutant finds no RHS entry for `wedged` and drops it, failing the block. Free coverage, correctly identified.
- **D5's priming rationale is correct and matches precedent** (`names.rs:127-131`, `:186-188`, `pg_outbox_listener.rs:123-125`): an unprimed counter that sees exactly one increment in the window has `increase() == 0` and would blind the control. Keep the reasoning even if the prime moves to `main.rs`.
- **§4.1's "prove each new block flips SUCCESS → FAILED when its control is deleted" discipline** and §3.1's insistence on the `ALL` entry (backed by `tests/drift.rs:165-181`) are exactly the right guards for this class of change.
Substantive critique. Let me verify the load-bearing claims myself before folding anything in.
